_meta.source: SkillsFuture Singapore Skills Frameworks for the sector and role structures; ITE, polytechnic and autonomous university Graduate Employment Surveys for the pay bands; Ministry of Manpower occupational wage data
_meta.units: Singapore dollars, gross monthly, for a first job
_meta.notes: Pay is stated ONCE per level of entry and never per sector. Sector by sector figures would be dozens of numbers this build cannot defend, and comparing sectors on pay is a prestige ranking wearing a dollar sign, which this app does not render. Every band is provisional and needs a human against the named surveys before a class sees it. Sectors are ordered alphabetically by label so the ordering is visibly arbitrary. Every sector carries a real entry at three or more levels, which is checked, because the claim that a level of entry is not a ceiling is the load bearing claim of this file.

levelPay.label: Fresh Nitec
levelPay.note: Higher with shift work, allowances, or a licence the job needs.

levelPay.label: Fresh Higher Nitec
levelPay.note: The third year at ITE is what moves this, and it also opens the poly door.

levelPay.label: Fresh polytechnic diploma
levelPay.note: Men who have served usually start a little above this, being two years older.

levelPay.label: Fresh degree from a local university
levelPay.note: The spread inside this is wider than the gap to the row above it.

sectors.label: Arts, performance and culture
sectors.isWhat: Making and staging work that people watch, hear or walk through, and running the places where that happens.
dayLooks: Rehearse the same eight bars
Hang and light a show
Run a workshop for schools

entries.route: Nitec in media or events production
entries.note: Sound, lighting and stage crew are hired on skill, not on a certificate.

entries.route: Diploma in arts management or performance
entries.note: The people who make shows happen outnumber the people on stage.

entries.route: NAFA or LASALLE, entry by audition or portfolio
entries.note: Entry turns on what I can do in the room, not on an aggregate.

entries.route: Degree in arts, history or education
entries.note: Museums, arts education and policy all hire from here.

sectors.licence: No licence gates this. A body of work that somebody can see does the same job.
sectors.moving: The audience is not shrinking and the funding moves. Arts education, community arts and the technical trades behind a stage are the steadier ground.
sectors.myth: That it is a hobby with a job attached. The National Arts Council, the venues and the schools all employ people full time, all year.
thisTerm: Get one piece in front of somebody who is not family
Ask a venue if they take student crew

sectors.label: Beauty, wellness and sport
sectors.isWhat: Working on people's bodies, appearance and fitness, in salons, gyms, spas, clinics and clubs.
dayLooks: Take a client through a programme
Do the treatment and the aftercare
Keep the books and the stock

entries.route: Nitec in beauty and wellness, or a sport certificate
entries.note: This sector genuinely starts here and a lot of owners started here too.

entries.route: Diploma in sport, exercise or applied science
entries.note: Opens rehabilitation, testing and the clubs that hire on science.

entries.route: Degree in physiotherapy, sport science or nutrition
entries.note: Clinical roles need this, and they are licensed on top of it.

sectors.licence: The sport coaching registry and the treatment certifications are what let somebody charge properly.
sectors.moving: An older population and a country that keeps building sport facilities. Rehabilitation and older adult fitness are growing faster than the aesthetics side.
sectors.myth: That it has no ladder. Salon and gym owners, franchise operators and clinical specialists all come out of the same first year on the floor.
thisTerm: Shadow one session at a gym, salon or clinic
Ask what a first year on the floor is really like

sectors.label: Building and what gets built
sectors.isWhat: Turning drawings into buildings, roads, tunnels and rail, and keeping them standing afterwards.
dayLooks: Walk a site against the drawings
Price a variation order
Coordinate three trades in one week

entries.route: Higher Nitec in architectural or facility technology
entries.note: Site experience counts here in a way a certificate does not replace.

entries.route: Diploma in built environment or civil engineering
entries.note: Most of this sector's hiring in volume happens at this level.

entries.route: Degree in civil engineering or architecture
entries.note: Signing off a structure needs a registered professional, and registration comes later.

sectors.licence: The Building and Construction Authority certifications, and Professional Engineer registration for the people who sign.
sectors.moving: Less swinging a hammer and more coordinating models, prefabrication and data. The work is not going anywhere and the tools change every few years.
sectors.myth: That it means the site only. Quantity surveying, project management, digital modelling and facilities all sit in offices and pay on responsibility.
thisTerm: Ask a site office what a coordinator actually does all day
Look up one Higher Nitec built environment course

sectors.label: Business, money and accounts
sectors.isWhat: Keeping track of what an organisation owns and owes, and deciding where the money goes next.
dayLooks: Close the month
Explain a variance to somebody senior
Check a client against the rules

entries.route: Nitec or Higher Nitec in business services
entries.note: The finance function of every organisation hires at this level.

entries.route: Diploma in accountancy, banking or business
entries.note: A route into the same firms, and part time degrees are normal after it.

entries.route: Degree in accountancy, business or economics
entries.note: The professional qualification is what matters after, not the degree alone.

sectors.licence: The Singapore Chartered Accountant qualification, or CFA on the investment side. Both are taken while working.
sectors.moving: Routine bookkeeping is being automated and the judgement work is not. Anti money laundering, sustainability reporting and advisory keep growing.
sectors.myth: That it is only for the arithmetic quick. It runs on being organised, asking a question when a number looks wrong, and explaining it clearly.
thisTerm: Keep an honest budget for one month and see what it teaches
Ask somebody in finance what they actually do at month end

sectors.label: Care, health and getting better
sectors.isWhat: Looking after people who are ill, injured, ageing or recovering, in hospitals, clinics, homes and their own flats.
dayLooks: Take a round of observations
Explain a diagnosis to a family
Run the equipment nobody else can

entries.route: Higher Nitec in nursing or healthcare
entries.note: There is a real ladder from here to enrolled nurse and beyond.

entries.route: Diploma in nursing or health sciences
entries.note: This is the main door into the hospitals, in volume, every year.

entries.route: Degree in medicine, pharmacy or allied health
entries.note: Longest run up, and the ladder from a diploma reaches here too.

sectors.licence: Registration with the Singapore Nursing Board, or the relevant professional board. The registration is the job, not the certificate.
sectors.moving: An ageing population means this sector grows for the next twenty years whatever else happens. Community and home care are growing faster than hospitals.
sectors.myth: That a diploma nurse is stuck. Nurses go on to degrees, to specialist practice and to advanced practice, most of it paid for while working.
thisTerm: Volunteer one term at a nursing home or a hospital
Ask a nurse what the first year was actually like

sectors.label: Children, teaching and learning
sectors.isWhat: Teaching, and looking after children while they learn, from eighteen months old to eighteen years.
dayLooks: Plan a week that actually holds
Sit with the one who is stuck
Talk to a parent honestly

entries.route: Higher Nitec in early childhood education
entries.note: A recognised route into a preschool, with a ladder to teacher after.

entries.route: Diploma in early childhood education
entries.note: The main qualification the sector hires on, and it is in demand.

entries.route: Degree, then the National Institute of Education
entries.note: The Ministry sponsors this, and a diploma route into teaching exists too.

sectors.licence: The Early Childhood Development Agency certification for preschool, and registration through the National Institute of Education for schools.
sectors.moving: More places, longer hours and higher qualifications expected. Special educational needs support and early intervention are the parts short of people.
sectors.myth: That it is minding children. Early years work is where the largest differences in a life get made, and the sector knows it and pays accordingly now.
thisTerm: Help at a childcare or a reading programme for one term
Ask a preschool teacher what surprised them most

sectors.label: Computing, data and keeping it safe
sectors.isWhat: Building the software people use, moving and making sense of data, and stopping other people breaking in.
dayLooks: Find why it broke overnight
Turn messy data into one answer
Patch what the scan found

entries.route: Higher Nitec in infocomm technology
entries.note: Hands on infrastructure and support work, and a real ladder from it.

entries.route: Diploma in information technology or data
entries.note: Employers here hire on what somebody has built, which a diploma has time for.

entries.route: Degree in computing, data science or engineering
entries.note: Deeper theory, and the research and platform roles start here.

sectors.licence: Nothing licenses this. Vendor certifications and a public portfolio of things that work do the same job.
sectors.moving: The tools change constantly and the demand does not. Anything that only follows instructions is being automated; anything that decides what to build is not.
sectors.myth: That a degree is the only door. This is the sector most willing to hire on demonstrated skill, and the most awkward about it in the first interview.
thisTerm: Build one small thing and put it somewhere public
Enter one hackathon or coding competition

sectors.label: Design, media and how it looks
sectors.isWhat: Deciding how a thing looks, reads and feels, then making the files that get it produced.
dayLooks: Take a brief apart before starting
Show three options, not one
Fix the version the client broke

entries.route: Nitec in visual communication or media
entries.note: Production skill first, which is what studios are short of.

entries.route: Diploma in design, media or animation
entries.note: The standard door, and the portfolio it produces is what gets hired.

entries.route: NAFA or LASALLE, entry by portfolio
entries.note: Studio hours and critique, with entry on the work rather than a score.

entries.route: Degree in design or communications
entries.note: Strategy, research and the teaching side of design sit here.

sectors.licence: None. Nobody has ever asked a designer for a licence. They ask to see the work.
sectors.moving: Generative tools took the bottom off the routine production work and raised what a client expects. Deciding what to make is the part that survived.
sectors.myth: That it is about being good at drawing. It is about understanding a problem and choosing, and the drawing is how the choice gets shown.
thisTerm: Redesign one real thing badly made and show both
Put four finished pieces where somebody can see them

sectors.label: Engineering and precision work
sectors.isWhat: Designing, building, testing and repairing machines, aircraft, ships, plants and the parts inside them.
dayLooks: Strip it, measure it, find the fault
Hold a tolerance nobody can see
Sign the maintenance record

entries.route: Nitec or Higher Nitec in engineering or aerospace
entries.note: Aerospace, marine and precision all hire heavily and directly at this level.

entries.route: Diploma in mechanical, electrical or aerospace engineering
entries.note: Design, testing and supervision, with a real route to a degree after.

entries.route: Degree in mechanical, electrical or chemical engineering
entries.note: The design and research end, and eventual professional registration.

sectors.licence: Aviation authority licences for aircraft work, and the plant and safety certifications the process industries require.
sectors.moving: Automation, semiconductors and the energy transition are pulling hard. The trades that keep complicated machines running are the hardest to fill.
sectors.myth: That it means dirty hands and low pay. Licensed aircraft engineers and process technicians are among the better paid people who never sat a degree.
thisTerm: Take one broken thing apart and get it working
Ask an ITE aerospace student what the licence takes

sectors.label: Food, from growing it to serving it
sectors.isWhat: Growing, making, cooking and serving what people eat, in farms, factories, kitchens and shops.
dayLooks: Prep before anybody arrives
Hold the same standard four hundred times
Cost a menu that has to work

entries.route: Nitec in culinary arts or food technology
entries.note: Kitchens hire on skill and attitude, and this is the fastest way to both.

entries.route: Diploma in food science, nutrition or hospitality
entries.note: The factory, safety and product development side, which is bigger than kitchens.

entries.route: Degree in food science or business
entries.note: Product development, regulation and running the operations at scale.

sectors.licence: The food hygiene certification to work at all, and the food safety qualifications that let somebody run a line.
sectors.moving: Local production, alternative proteins and automation in the back kitchen. The hours in food service are hard and the sector knows it is a problem.
sectors.myth: That it is a job for now and not a career. Food manufacturing, safety and product development are quiet, technical and steady, and few students know they exist.
thisTerm: Work one service in a real kitchen and see
Read the label on something I eat weekly and look up two ingredients

sectors.label: Hotels, travel and looking after guests
sectors.isWhat: Running the places people stay, eat, fly through and visit, and the events that fill them.
dayLooks: Turn a complaint into a returning guest
Run a floor with people short
Build an event minute by minute

entries.route: Nitec in hospitality operations
entries.note: This sector promotes from the floor faster than most, if somebody is good.

entries.route: Diploma in hospitality or tourism management
entries.note: The management track, and the internships are real work in real hotels.

entries.route: Degree in hospitality or business
entries.note: Revenue, brand and regional roles, and the analysis behind the pricing.

sectors.licence: None to enter. The languages somebody speaks and the systems they can run are what move them.
sectors.moving: Travel came back and the staffing did not. That is uncomfortable for the people inside and it means the ladder is unusually short right now.
sectors.myth: That it is smiling at people. It is running a complicated operation on thin margins with a queue watching, which is a genuinely hard skill.
thisTerm: Work one event as crew and watch how it is run
Ask a hotel duty manager what goes wrong most

sectors.label: Law, safety and public service
sectors.isWhat: Making, applying and enforcing the rules, and running the services a country needs to work.
dayLooks: Read the file until the point appears
Make a decision somebody will contest
Hold a scene together

entries.route: Nitec, then Police, Civil Defence or Prisons intake
entries.note: The uniformed services recruit and train at this level, with a real ladder.

entries.route: Diploma in law and management or public administration
entries.note: Legal support, statutory boards and the specialist officer schemes.

entries.route: Degree in law, or any degree for the service
entries.note: Practice needs the law degree and a training contract after it.

sectors.licence: Admission to the Singapore Bar for practice, and the service specific training and warrants for the uniformed roles.
sectors.moving: More technology and data protection work, more compliance across every sector, and a public service that hires on skill from a widening set of places.
sectors.myth: That the public service only takes degree holders. The uniformed services and the statutory boards run specialist and officer schemes at every level.
thisTerm: Read one real judgment and see how the reasoning runs
Ask a serving officer about the first two years

sectors.label: Moving things and people
sectors.isWhat: Getting cargo, ships, aircraft, trains and buses where they need to be, on time, at the right cost.
dayLooks: Solve a delay before anybody notices
Load a plan that has to balance
Keep a fleet running to a schedule

entries.route: Nitec or Higher Nitec in logistics or engineering
entries.note: The rail and air operators recruit and train heavily at this level.

entries.route: Diploma in logistics, aviation or maritime studies
entries.note: Planning and coordination, in a sector where Singapore is a world hub.

entries.route: Degree in supply chain, maritime or engineering
entries.note: Network design, chartering and the analytical end of the same work.

sectors.licence: The dangerous goods, port and aviation certifications, and the professional maritime qualifications for the ship side.
sectors.moving: Automation in the port and the warehouse, and a lot more data. Singapore's position as a hub is the most durable economic fact about the place.
sectors.myth: That it means driving a lorry. It means deciding what moves and when, on systems that touch a fifth of the world's transhipment.
thisTerm: Track one parcel and work out every hand it passed through
Ask somebody at the port or the airport what a shift is like

sectors.label: Selling, shops and what people want
sectors.isWhat: Working out what people will buy, getting it in front of them, and running the places and sites where it happens.
dayLooks: Read yesterday's numbers and change today
Talk somebody through a real decision
Fill a shelf that tells a story

entries.route: Nitec in retail services or business
entries.note: Fastest sector to get real responsibility young, if somebody wants it.

entries.route: Diploma in retail, marketing or business
entries.note: Buying, planning and the digital side, which is where the sector moved.

entries.route: Degree in business or marketing
entries.note: Strategy, pricing and the analysis behind what gets stocked at all.

sectors.licence: None. A record of having sold something difficult is what people actually ask about.
sectors.moving: The physical shop is now part of a system that includes a phone and a warehouse. The people who understand both halves are short.
sectors.myth: That a shop job is not a career. Buyers, merchandise planners and country managers overwhelmingly started on a floor and can tell you what week they learned it.
thisTerm: Sell something I made or sourced and count what happened
Ask a store manager how they decide what goes where

sectors.label: Social work and people in trouble
sectors.isWhat: Working with people whose lives have come apart, and with the families and systems around them.
dayLooks: Sit with somebody at their worst
Write the case note that decides funding
Argue for one family in a meeting

entries.route: Higher Nitec in community care
entries.note: Front line work in family services and community organisations.

entries.route: Diploma in social sciences or community development
entries.note: Casework support and programme work, with a route to the degree after.

entries.route: Degree in social work or psychology
entries.note: Casework accountability and clinical practice need this and registration.

sectors.licence: Registration with the Singapore Association of Social Workers for accredited practice, and the counselling body for counsellors.
sectors.moving: Funded properly for the first time in a while, and short of people. Mental health and elder care are the parts growing fastest.
sectors.myth: That it is charity work with a stipend. It is a registered profession with supervision, caseload standards and a salary the sector has deliberately raised.
thisTerm: Volunteer somewhere uncomfortable for one term
Ask a social worker what they wish somebody had told them

sectors.label: The environment and keeping things running
sectors.isWhat: Water, waste, energy, cleaning, pest control and the systems inside every building that nobody notices until they stop.
dayLooks: Read the plant and act on it
Audit a building against its numbers
Fix what forty people depend on

entries.route: Higher Nitec in facility or environmental technology
entries.note: Essential work with a shortage of people, and shift allowances on top.

entries.route: Diploma in environmental or facility management
entries.note: The reporting and management side, which every large organisation now needs.

entries.route: Degree in environmental engineering or science
entries.note: Design of treatment, energy and climate systems, and the policy side.

sectors.licence: The environmental and water treatment operator certifications, and the green building accreditations for the reporting side.
sectors.moving: Sustainability reporting became compulsory for large firms, which created a profession that barely existed ten years ago. Water and waste never stop.
sectors.myth: That it is cleaning. It is the reason the water is drinkable and the building is cool, and it is run by people with instruments and certificates.
thisTerm: Find out where my estate's water and waste actually go
Ask a building manager what breaks most often
